newsitem.title: GERMANY: Karstadt sales slightly down in '96.
newsitem.headline: Karstadt sales slightly down in '96.

text.p: German department store group Karstadt AG said on Wednesday that group sales for 1996 fell by 0.3 percent to 26.9 billion marks ($16.9 billion), but said a magazine report that it had lost money was unfounded.

Addressing a report by news magazine Wirtschaftswoche, which quoted an internal forecast that its department stores lost 300 million marks, Karstadt said "no such forecast exists, either for the department stores or for the group as a whole." ($ = 1.594 German Marks)
Karstadt said that it would publish its final results this spring, as usual.
Parent company Karstadt AG raised sales at its 186 stores by two percent to 12.32 billion, including value-added tax. Same-store sales, however, were down by 1.1 percent.

The struggling Hertie Waren- und Kaufhaus GmbH chain suffered a fall in turnover of 15.6 percent to 4.2 billion marks, mainly due to the transfer of 16 branches to Karstadt and the closure of a further 10 stores.
Sales on a same-store basis at Hertie were down 5.3 percent.
Among other key units, mail order operation Neckermann Versand AG raised sales by three percent to 3.35 billion marks, including VAT.
And NUR Touristic GmbH increased sales by 6.9 percent to 3.6 billion marks in the business year to October 31, Karstadt said.
